window: Covering reporting published since the Sept 13 edition, roughly Sept 12-14, with South American incident dates running back to Sept 10 where Spanish-language reporting lagged. No federal-level US story surfaced that wasn't already logged: DEA's press-release feed has posted nothing new since Sept 9 (the Rockland, Massachusetts opioid case already in the last edition), and a search across CBP, Coast Guard, DOJ/USAO and Treasury/OFAC turned up nothing from this window that was both new and substantial — the federal section is empty today rather than padded with stale filler. Excluded after verification: a recirculating 'DEA-led raid off Ecuador nets 3,284 kilos of cocaine' story, still sourced only to an undated DEA social-media post with no named agencies, date or location, excluded from the last two editions for the same reason; a California DOJ 'Santa Ana trafficker' release that read as breaking news but is a 2023 case being recirculated; a Kansas City fentanyl/carfentanil indictment already logged Sept 3; an India Mizoram seizure already logged Sept 11 (same article, re-surfaced in search); and several Pakistani ANF and Argentine Gendarmeria seizures that were day-to-day repeats of a pattern already represented in the log this month. No new development emerged on the SOUTHCOM boat-strike or refueling-vessel campaigns (SOUTHCOM's press page has posted nothing since the Sept 9 strike already logged), the Los Tiguerones case, Uruguay's Artigas airdrop case or Bolivia's aircraft-grounding crackdown, so the ongoing section is empty again.
